title: The four levels of organization
blurb: Define the business layer, directing, managing and delivering levels, and explain why the project management team is only the three inside the project.
question: Which level of organization provides the project mandate and identifies the executive?

teach.h: Four levels, three inside the project
teach.body: Formally: the project management structure has four levels. Three of them (directing, managing and delivering) make up the project management team; the fourth, the business layer, sits outside the project. In plain English: the business commissions and sets the outer limits, the board steers, the project manager runs it day to day, and the teams build the products.

teach.caption: The project management team (PMT) is the three blue levels.

head: Level
Who
Key job
rows: Accountable for success; directs within limits
Manage their element within PM limits
teach.caption: Each level works within constraints set by the level above it.
A forecast breach goes back up to the level that set the limit.

teach.h: Managing and delivering, in v7 words
teach.body: The project manager's primary responsibility is to manage the relationships within the project so it produces the products in line with the strategic objectives and the agreed requirements. Team managers and members manage and decide day to day for their element, co-creating where needed with others across the project ecosystem.

teach.caption: The board is accountable TO the business layer for the project's success.

teach.body: Cobalt Bay Ferries' executive committee (business layer) issues a mandate for new ticket gates, names operations director Ines Ward as executive and sets project tolerances of plus or minus 10% on cost. Ines's board sets each stage's tolerances. Project manager Kofi Mensah sets work package tolerances for two team managers: one installing gates, one configuring software. When a supplier delay threatens the project end date beyond its tolerance, the decision goes up to the executive committee.

teach.text: Trap: the business layer is NOT part of the project management team. In the 6th edition it was called 'corporate, programme management or the customer'; PRINCE2 7 calls it the business layer. A breach of project tolerance is decided by the business layer, not by the board alone.

items: Four levels: business layer, directing, managing, delivering.
The PMT is the three inside the project; the business layer is outside it.
Business layer: mandate, identifies the executive, project tolerances.
Board sets stage tolerances; PM sets work package tolerances.

summary: You can now name the four levels of organization, say what each one does and which tolerances it sets. You can also explain why the business layer sits outside the project management team.

A.q: Which level of organization sits outside the project management team?
A.why: The business layer commissions the project and sits outside the project management team (6.2, fig 6.2).

whyNot.0: Directing (the project board) is inside the project management team.
whyNot.1: Managing (the project manager) is inside the project management team.
whyNot.3: Delivering (team managers) is inside the project management team.

A.q: Which level of organization does the project board represent?
A.why: The project board works at the directing level.

whyNot.0: Managing is the project manager's level.
whyNot.1: Commissioning is the business layer, outside the project management team.
whyNot.3: Delivering is the level of team managers and team members.

A.why: The business layer defines the project-level tolerances within which the project board works.

whyNot.0: The board sets stage tolerances within the project tolerances.
whyNot.1: The project manager sets work package tolerances.
whyNot.2: The senior user is a board member and does not set project tolerances.

B.q:
Which two statements about the levels of organization are correct?
1. The project management team comprises the directing, managing and delivering levels.
2. The business layer provides the project mandate.
3. The project board sets work package tolerances.
4. Team managers set stage tolerances.
B.why: The PMT is the three levels inside the project (1), and the commissioning business layer provides the mandate (2).

whyNot.1: Statement 3 is false: the project manager sets work package tolerances.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is false: the project board sets stage tolerances.
whyNot.3: Both are false: the PM sets work package tolerances and the board sets stage tolerances.

B.q: What is the project manager's primary responsibility at the managing level?
options: Securing the funding needed for the whole project
Managing relationships so products meet requirements
Setting the tolerances for each management stage
Approving the project mandate before starting up
B.why: The PM's primary responsibility is managing relationships within the project so it produces the products in line with strategic objectives and agreed requirements.

whyNot.0: Securing funding is the executive's responsibility.
whyNot.2: Stage tolerances are set by the project board.
whyNot.3: The project mandate comes from the business layer before starting up.

B.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. Team managers and team members work at the [?] level, managing their element of the project within constraints set by the project manager.
B.why: Team managers and members are the delivering level.

C.q: Which level identifies the executive, and which level does the executive then work at?
C.why: The commissioning business layer identifies the executive, who then sits on the project board at the directing level.

whyNot.0: The order is reversed: the business layer identifies the executive, who joins the board.
whyNot.2: The executive is a board member (directing), not at the managing level.
whyNot.3: The project manager does not identify the executive.

C.q: A forecast shows the project will exceed its project-level cost tolerance. Which level decides what happens, and why?
options: Business layer, as it set the project tolerances
Project board, as it directs the whole project
Project manager, as they run it day to day
Team manager, as their team incurred the cost
C.why: Breaches of project tolerance go to the business layer, the level that set the project tolerances.

whyNot.1: The board directs within project tolerances; a forecast breach of them goes to the business layer.
whyNot.2: The PM escalates beyond stage tolerance to the board; they cannot decide on project tolerance.
whyNot.3: Team managers work within work package tolerances and escalate to the PM.

C.q: Which level sets work package tolerances, and for whom?
C.why: The project manager (managing level) sets work package tolerances and constraints for team managers.

whyNot.0: The board sets stage tolerances, not work package tolerances.
whyNot.1: Tolerances flow down: the delivering level does not set them for the PM.
whyNot.2: The board's tolerances are set by the business layer, not by the PM.

reteach.title: A school trip has four levels
reteach.question: Who decides a school trip can go ahead, who leads it on the day, and who looks after each group?

blocks.body: The governors approve the trip and set the budget limit (business layer). A trip committee of the head, a parent rep and the coach firm steers it (directing). The trip leader runs the day (managing). Each group leader looks after their group (delivering). Only the last three are on the trip itself.

blocks.text: The governors set the overall limits but are not part of the trip team, just as the business layer is outside the project management team.

explain.body: Business layer, directing, managing and delivering. Each works within limits set by the level above.

test.q: How many levels of organization are there, including the business layer?
test.why: There are four levels: business layer, directing, managing and delivering.

whyNot.0: Three is the number inside the project management team, not the total.
whyNot.2: There is no fifth level; project assurance and support are roles, not levels.
whyNot.3: Two levels would leave out managing and delivering.

explain.body: The project management team is the three levels inside the project: directing, managing and delivering. The business layer is outside it.

test.q: Which levels make up the project management team?
test.why: The PMT is the directing, managing and delivering levels.

whyNot.0: The business layer is outside the PMT, and delivering is missing.
whyNot.1: The business layer is outside the PMT.
whyNot.2: The project board (directing) is part of the PMT too.

explain.body: The business layer sets project tolerances, the board sets stage tolerances, and the PM sets work package tolerances.

test.why: The project board sets stage tolerances to enable management by exception.

whyNot.0: The business layer sets project tolerances.
whyNot.1: The project manager sets work package tolerances.
whyNot.3: The team manager sets limits for team members.

explain.body: The commissioning party provides the project mandate, identifies the executive and defines project-level tolerances.

test.q: Which is a responsibility of the business layer?
options: Running each stage day to day
test.why: The commissioning business layer provides the project mandate.

whyNot.1: The project manager authorizes work packages.
whyNot.3: The project manager runs each stage day to day.
